title: DR1 shows each transporter's type, approval status and a link to its full details; the frontend shows only a name, an address and an approval number.

finding.frontend: Each transporter is one radio whose label is the name and whose hint is the address and approval number run together — "43 East Hague Extension, …, Switzerland — approval number ES-T2-45001294" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:92-93). There is no type, no approval status and no way to see anything more about a transporter before choosing it. A user picking between two similar names has only the address to go on.
finding.prototype: The transporters are a table with a header row and six columns — Name, Address, Approval number, Type, Status and a per-row link (app/views/transporter.html:113-153). Type reads "Commercial" or "Private". Status is a coloured tag, "Approved" or "New". The last column is a "View details" link to that transporter's own page.
finding.difference: Render the transporter list as a table with the DR1 columns rather than as radio hints: add Type, add the approval-status tag, and add a per-row link to the transporter's details. The status tag needs a source of truth for whether a transporter is approved or newly added, which the frontend's fixed record list does not carry today (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:6-27), so that field has to be added to whatever supplies the list. Do it with the search field, which changes the same list.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a status, type or details link anywhere on fe-transporter-commercial — the captured DOM for that screen has one fieldset containing two radios and their hints, and no table element at all.

relatedTo.why: both rebuild the same transporter list
